goal: Implement Slice S2 of Initiative user-acceptance-scenarios: imm-tracker publish-initiative accepts optional per-Task scenarios, renders a 'User scenarios' section on the Child and a derived listing on the Parent, and rejects the whole batch before any remote write when a scenario is malformed or names an acceptance ID its TaskIntent lacks. A publication without scenarios renders byte-identical bodies; terminal projection, TaskIntent schema, and Kernel authority are unchanged.

acceptance.assertion: Per T4 and invariants I3 and I4 of docs/specs/user-acceptance-scenarios.spec.md (source: #186 D4, D7, D9, D10): given Tasks that supply scenarios, the Child body has '## User scenarios' after '## Acceptance criteria' with one item per own scenario showing its ID, mode, mapped acceptance IDs, and Actor, Given, When, Then, a manual scenario as an unchecked task-list item with its reason and an automated one as a plain bullet; and the Parent body has '## User scenarios' after '## Testing strategy' with one plain bullet per scenario of every Task showing its ID, owning Slice ID, mode, When, and Then (positive). A Child that supplies no scenario renders no such heading even when a sibling does (negative). When no Task supplies scenarios the Parent and every Child body are byte-identical to the bodies rendered without this feature; mark-terminal with phase done on a Child whose manual scenario box was ticked closes it as completed and preserves the tick; and an amendment leaves every historical Child's bytes untouched while a bound pending Child's scenarios update with its brief (bound).

Per T5 of docs/specs/user-acceptance-scenarios.spec.md (source: #186 D8, D11): a batch whose scenarios are a valid mix of automated and manual entries publishes (positive). It performs zero mutating remote calls and returns its existing structured failure, naming Task and scenario or acceptance ID, for a scenario that lacks a required field, has an id not matching BR-SCN-<n> or SCN-<n>, repeats an id within the Initiative, is automated with no acceptance ID, names an acceptance ID absent from its TaskIntent, or is manual without manual_reason (negative). A manual scenario naming no acceptance ID is accepted; scenario text obeys the existing public-projection text rules and bounds (bound). Every rendered scenario list item starts at line start, with no metadata comment before the bullet or task-list marker (positive). Each Child's ownership marker block carries one <!-- immune-brain:scenarios=<percent-encoded JSON> --> per Task, holding all its scenarios verbatim; manual_reason is required in manual mode, validated whenever supplied, and retained for either mode; an amendment reads each historical Child's scenarios only from its marker: a Child carrying no scenarios marker has no historical scenarios and its bytes are never rewritten; when a marker is present there must be exactly one with a complete frame, validated by the same validator as pending scenarios and re-encoding byte for byte equal to the marker, and any other state rejects the whole batch before any write (negative). Stored values must also survive re-projection, so a value grown past its bound by escaping, or a restricted-context acceptance ID the pending path accepts, is rejected at publish before any write (negative). Multiline text, Markdown headings, and Markdown bullets in scenario fields are data; a pending scenario repeating any historical ID is rejected before any write (negative).

Per T5 of docs/specs/user-acceptance-scenarios.spec.md (source: #186 D10, D11): the packaged Planner contract's Initiative Carrier Preference section and docs/agents/issue-tracker.md describe the optional per-Task scenarios input, its automated and manual modes, and that omitting it renders no section (positive); the text states scenarios are public projection that never widens TaskIntent scope or authority (negative); and the existing carrier-gate contract assertions are unchanged (bound).
